fact: The World Bank's identity diagnostic states that MASSAR was developed by the Ministry of National Education and Vocational Training (MENFP) over two and a half years and officially launched at the end of 2013; it gives no spending figure for it.

The diagnostic states that MASSAR's student register covers every child enrolled in any of the more than 10,000 national educational establishments, ages 6 to 18: 6,512,192 unique students as of May 2014, about 94 per cent of the 6.9 million children of that age, and by the World Bank's reckoning 98 per cent of children of primary age (6 to 10).

The diagnostic describes MASSAR as a fully electronic system for managing 'all aspects of the scholastic life' of children, in which each establishment registers and vets its own students into a central, cumulative database and each student receives a unique number kept for the whole of their schooling, with about 600,000 new entrants a year; it does not say that attendance or results are entered (assessment visit of June 2014).

The diagnostic states that MASSAR's central database is reached by secure access from 10,000 locations and that students are vetted at each of the country's 10,000 learning establishments, a figure for all levels aged 6 to 18 with no separate count of primary schools and no rural breakdown (assessment visit of June 2014).
